knowledge_gaps: The panel measures candidate-distribution sensitivity, but cannot identify why low-frequency targets have weaker separation or establish that changing training negatives will improve validation HR@10. Frequency matching does not isolate popularity bias.

Uncertainty is underspecified when a previously frozen uniform set becomes draw zero. Its provenance and independence from additional draws must be verified before applying independent-stream MCSE formulas. Five draws may poorly estimate maximum-negative-margin variability.

Reproduction requires an explicit user cap, case-protocol version, ordered candidate pools, serialized-ID collision handling, and rules for nonfinite draws and empty complete-case subsets. The supplied workflow and previous proposals describe different target-selection protocols.

Exact finite-population calculations could replace sampling noise for some statistics: the negative-win fraction has an exact pool expectation, and sampled outranking counts follow a hypergeometric distribution. Whether full-pool scoring warrants its runtime cost is unexplored.

The related-work descriptions need primary-source verification. Originality 4 is reasonable; future potential 7 is optimistic without a prespecified next training experiment, and difficulty 3 understates reproducibility and uncertainty work.
